input.quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
input.rationale: Section 15.3 contains a mutual cap and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, but the cap basis fails the fallback: 3% of the bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered over the entire term is far below twelve months' (or even six months') fees, so MSL's exposure is effectively illusory relative to the volume it manufactures for us. The cap is also expressed as covering "total liability ... regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort," with no carve-outs, so MSL's indemnities under Section 15.1 (third-party IP infringement, regulatory non-compliance, warranty support) and its confidentiality obligations sit inside this very low cap with no super-cap — the walk-away scenario in the rule. We therefore reset the basis to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and added a single carve-out sentence for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, plus confirmation that our payment obligations are not capped damages. Mutuality is preserved, so the edit does not disturb the existing bargain beyond the cap basis and carve-outs.

proposal.summary: Reset the mutual cap to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid/payable and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IBM's payment obligations outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reset the cap basis to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, because 3% of bill-of-materials value across the entire term sits well below our minimum of twelve months' fees. We also placed indemnification, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud outside the cap and confirmed payment obligations are not capped damages; if helpful, we can accept a straight twelve months' fees cap with these carve-outs as a fallback.

ops.oldText: is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
ops.newText: is limited to the greater of (i) the amounts paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the action and (ii) one million U.S. dollars (US$1,000,000). The limitations in this Section 15.3 do not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations under this Section 15.0, a Party's breach of its confidentiality or data security obligations, a Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, or a Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and IBM's obligation to pay amounts due for Products or services is not subject to this limitation.
